This SM is organized as follows. In the first section, we explain our choice of the numerical scheme that was used to produce the numerical results discussed in the main text. In the second section, we transform from Reiterer– Trubowitz to Martı́n-Garcı́a–Gundlach gauge. In the third section, we list the first three non-trivial orders in the large-D perturbation theory. In the fourth section, we construct an explicit large-D model that is exploited in the main text. On the final page, we display in Table I our numerical results of the echoing period in dimensions between 3.046 and 200; for comparison we added as a final entry our best-fit result for D → ∞. The results for D > 28 have sufficient accuracy so that we trust all displayed digits, and we checked that varying the number of Fourier or Chebyshev modes does not alter these digits. The results for D ≤ 5.5 contain also data from our previous work [29]. Choice of numerical scheme Choptuik’s original code evolved one-parameter families of initial data in time and checked whether or not there is an apparent horizon to decide if a black hole has formed. Using this code, he discovered the echoing period in D = 4 is approximately given by ∆Ch = 3.44 ± 10−2 . (S1) Variants of this approach were subsequently used by Sorkin and Oren [27] and Bland et al.
